data.title: SBF Lawyer Says $11 Billion Fine Would Leave Him Poor Forever
data.description: Sam Bankman-Fried’s Supreme Court lawyer says the $11 billion penalty tied to his sentence would leave the FTX founder broke for life after prison. According to BeInCrypto, Jeffrey Fisher argued the money judgment violates the Eighth Amendment ban on excessive fines and said no realistic future earnings could ever repay it. Fisher also said jurors heard customers lost billions but were not told they would be repaid, which he says denied SBF a fair trial.

data.title: Japan Ministries Propose Just 17 Billion Yen in Budget Cuts
data.description: According to Nikkei Asia, Japanese government ministries and agencies have proposed budget cuts totaling just 17 billion yen ($110 million) so far under Tokyo's version of the U.S. DOGE budget efficiency initiative. The figure suggests limited appetite in the bureaucracy for spending reductions.

data.title: SEC Chairman Urges Congress to Advance CLARITY Act
data.description: SEC Chairman urges Congress to advance the CLARITY Act and send it to the President's desk as soon as possible. According to NS3.AI, Project Crypto is the SEC's agency-wide effort to establish the United States as the Crypto Capital of the World. The SEC has also proposed Regulation Crypto Assets to create a legal framework for crypto projects. The chairman said the administration will deliver for investors and technological innovators with or without the legislation.

data.title: Stock Futures Near Flat Ahead Of Fed Policy Decision
data.description:
According to CNBC, U.S. stock futures were little changed Monday evening as traders awaited the Federal Reserve's policy decision later this week. S&P 500 futures rose 0.07%, Dow Jones Industrial Average futures gained 28 points, or 0.05%, and Nasdaq 100 futures advanced 0.08%.

In the regular session, the Dow fell 152 points, or 0.3%, the S&P 500 lost 0.5%, and the Nasdaq Composite slipped about 0.6%. AI-related stocks weighed on the market after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower pace of AI development, while OpenAI CEO Sam Altman ruled out an initial public offering this year. Nvidia dropped 3%, Corning tumbled 13%, and the iShares AI Innovation and Tech Active ETF (BAI) fell nearly 4%.

The 10-year Treasury yield briefly topped 5% for its highest level since October 2023, while Brent futures closed above $105 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate crude settled over $101 after Saudi Arabia shuttered a key pipeline that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz. Fed funds futures imply about a 92% chance the central bank will raise rates by a quarter point from the current target range of 3.5% to 3.75%.

data.title: McConnell Returns to Capitol After 3-Month Absence Following Fall
data.description:
According to CNBC, Sen. Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., returned to the Capitol on Monday after a three-month absence following a fall that left him hospitalized and out of public view for 92 days. McConnell said he had assured Senate Majority Leader John Thune that he would do his best to be present for tough votes when Republicans need him, and said in a statement that he would cast his first Senate vote since taking a bad fall back in June. He said he was looking forward to being back on the Senate floor and seeing his colleagues.

The 84-year-old former Senate Republican leader had not been seen publicly since he was hospitalized June 14. He had not cast a Senate vote since June 11 and missed dozens of votes during his absence. McConnell said his recovery has been a long and often frustrating process, that lingering effects of childhood polio have complicated it, and that he is still not quite back to 100% and will continue physical therapy on doctors' advice. His return restores another available vote for Republicans, who hold a 53-47 Senate majority.

data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, OpenAI top lobbyist Lehane met with lawmakers on Capitol Hill on Monday and also planned to meet with congressional leadership.

data.title: Macro Risk Advisors LLC Sees Fed Rate Hike Risking S&P 500 Pullback
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Macro Risk Advisors LLC said a possible Federal Reserve rate hike this week could trigger a pullback in the S&P 500 Index, as narrowing corporate profit margins would hit earnings prospects and markets prepare for a new tightening cycle.

data.title: Senate Democrats Plan Clarity Act Strategy Meeting Ahead of First Major Test
data.description: Senate Democrats are expected to meet tonight to discuss their strategy on the Clarity Act and coordinate a counterproposal to the text Republicans released last night, according to a Fox Business crypto reporter on X. According to Odaily, Republicans said the text was their "last, best and final" offer, and the bill will face its first major test on the Senate floor in less than 24 hours.

data.title: Zelenskyy Says Ukraine Is Ready to Support De-Escalation After U.S. Proposal
data.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine is willing to support de-escalation if the United States can ensure Russia is truly prepared to stop what he called a war aimed at destroying lives. According to Sina Finance, Zelenskyy said a strong U.S. proposal for both sides to stop striking critical infrastructure could be the first step toward easing tensions and ending Russian attacks on Ukraine's critical infrastructure, as well as Ukraine's response actions.

He said that if the United States can ensure Russia takes de-escalation measures, Ukraine will also take corresponding steps. Zelenskyy added that energy, grain transport routes, and critical infrastructure must all be included in discussions on stopping strikes, and said Ukraine needs a strong and fair solution that is not just for an election but resolves the issue once and for all.

data.title: AI | McKinsey’s Kate Smaje Says Boardrooms Are Focused on AI Scale and Profitability
data.description:
Kate Smaje of McKinsey said warnings from AI leaders and researchers about slowing development are fueling an important debate over AGI, risk, pace and patience. Bloomberg reported she said the discussion in boardrooms is different, with executives who have already invested heavily in AI now focused on whether the tools can scale, deliver profitability and remain sustainable.

She made the comments on "The Close" with Romaine Bostick and Isabelle Lee, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: U.S. Air Force Secretary Says U.S. Has “On-Orbit” Space Control Weapons
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, U.S. Air Force Secretary Troy Meink said at the annual Aerospace, Space and Cyber Conference in Maryland that the United States already has “on-orbit” space control weapons, and The Washington Post reported that this was the first U.S. acknowledgment of “offensive capabilities” in space.

data.title: Trump Calls AI Data Centers the 'Oil of the Next 20, 25 Years'
data.description: According to CNBC, U.S. President Donald Trump said AI data centers are the "oil of the next 20, 25 years" after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang put him on speakerphone during Huang's appearance at the All-in Summit in Los Angeles. Trump also said the concerns around AI and data centers are a "hoax" and a "scam," argued that additional AI regulation is unnecessary, and praised data center construction as a source of wealth for states and people. He told Huang, "I'm with you all the way," while Huang replied, "We're not going to let that happen, sir."

data.title: Costco Limits Motor Oil Purchases As Prices Rise
data.description:
According to CNBC, Costco has imposed purchase limits on some motor oil products and raised prices as crude oil markets tighten. The warehouse club set a limit of one transaction per membership, with a maximum of two units every seven days, on its Kirkland Signature full synthetic motor oil two-pack, which now costs $57.99, up from a typical range near $30. Sales of Mobil 1 motor oil on Costco's website are also capped at five per membership at $43.99 for a six-pack of 1-quart bottles.

Brent crude traded above $109 per barrel Monday morning before closing at $105.68 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate settled at $101.39 a barrel after trading above $104 earlier in the day. The article said the rise in oil prices has been driven by conflict in the Middle East, including Saudi Arabia's closure of its key East-West oil pipeline after drone attacks launched from Iraq damaged parts of it last week. It also said tighter oil supply has boosted refiners' profits on finished fuels such as diesel and gasoline, encouraging them to favor fuel production over base oil, a key ingredient in synthetic motor oil.

data.title: Iran's Mohsen Rezaei: Do Not Be Misled by Contradictory U.S. Signals
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Iran's Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei said not to be misled by contradictory signals from U.S. President Donald Trump, from "no negotiations" to "we are ready to talk." He said the stakes around oil and the strait have changed, crisis management cannot stop what is coming, and no talks will be held until Iran's conditions are met.

data.title: Bitcoin News | Bitcoin Hits $79,000 With Fed Hike Odds at 92.7%
data.description: Bitcoin returned above $79,000 after Monday's Wall Street open, gaining around 3% on the day as markets dissected mixed signals over the US-Iran war.The move followed comments from President Donald Trump raising prospects of a peace deal."The failing Nation of Iran wants to make a deal, quickly and badly. I will determine whether or not the U.S.A. will choose to engage — The concept of which we are open to," he wrote on Truth Social.The Two 50-Week Lines Sit $3,650 ApartBitcoin returned above its 50-week exponential moving average at $77,430 after initially closing the weekly candle below it. The 50-week EMA is a key support target for a bull-market comeback.That line is distinct from the 50-week simple moving average at $81,081, which rejected Bitcoin at an $81,265 intraday high in late August and has not been cleared since.The gap between them is roughly $3,650, and Bitcoin currently sits between the two. The EMA weights recent prices more heavily, which pulls it lower during a drawdown and makes it the first line reclaimed on a recovery. The SMA is the slower, more demanding test.Reclaiming the EMA is a real technical event. It is not the same event as clearing the SMA, and coverage that refers to "the 50-week moving average" without specifying which one is describing two different levels interchangeably.Oil Dipped but Remains Above $100Trump doubled down in a separate post: "With the temporary exception of Oil, prices are coming down sharply, and Oil will drop like a rock as soon as the Military Conflict with Iran is over, and that will not be long."Prices dipped on the comments. WTI remained above $100 a barrel and Brent traded at $105.That is a prediction rather than a policy action, and the physical constraints have not changed. Three major transit routes remain under threat — the Strait of Hormuz, Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and the Bab El-Mandeb Strait.The pipeline closure is the structural item. It runs to the Red Sea port of Yanbu and exists to bypass Hormuz. With Hormuz disrupted and the bypass shut, Saudi crude has no unconstrained export route, and production fell to 6.238 million barrels per day — the lowest since 1990.Bab El-Mandeb coming under threat closes the remaining alternative. A tanker routed to Yanbu to avoid Hormuz still has to pass Bab El-Mandeb to reach European markets.US equities initially gained at the open before turning red, with the S&P 500 down 0.3% amid ongoing uncertainty over those routes.Hike Odds Ran From 59.4% to 92.7% in a WeekCME FedWatch puts the probability of a 25 basis point increase at 92.7%, up from 59.4% a week ago.Markets expect the move to take the target range to 3.75%-4.00% from 3.50%-3.75%.QCP Capital identified the policy bind the energy shock creates."A prolonged disruption would increase the risk of higher energy costs feeding into transport and logistics pricing, potentially lifting inflation expectations and constraining the Fed's ability to pause tightening even as growth slows," the firm wrote.It added: "This dynamic creates policy tension: continued energy prices could keep the Fed restrictive, while economic data weakness from higher energy costs could argue for patience."That is the sharpest statement of why Wednesday is difficult. An energy shock is inflationary and contractionary simultaneously, and the two implications point in opposite policy directions.The Language Matters More Than the DecisionQCP argued risk assets have already priced the 25 basis point move, with less volatility expected as a result.It pointed to the muted response to last week's CPI data as evidence that Fed officials' framing now carries more weight than the decision."This containment reflects a shift in focus: the binary question of whether the Fed will hike has been answered; the critical issue for positioning is now how policymakers frame the move and what it signals about the path ahead."The gap between market pricing and house forecasts is where that plays out. Markets price roughly 3.5 hikes long term. Bank of America and RBC Capital Markets both expect 75 basis points this year. Jefferies expects fewer, with Mohit Kumar arguing the first move is a credibility matter while subsequent ones depend on the war's duration and oil prices.The dot plot either validates the market path or corrects it. Chair Kevin Warsh has to deliver that signal without doing the forward guidance he rejected at Jackson Hole — the projections provide it impersonally, which may be the intended route.Positioning Is Light Going InSantiment data shows BTC-denominated open contracts fell 13.5% between September 3 and 11, against a 5% price decline. Positioning sits roughly 20% below pre-rally levels.Deleveraging stopped on September 11 — CPI day — and rebounded slightly over the two following sessions, suggesting the reduction was preparatory rather than forced.That limits the liquidation cascade available in either direction Wednesday. It also means less short-covering fuel if the surprise arrives.Above Bitcoin, Glassnode data shows nearly 8% of supply was acquired between $80,000 and $82,000 — the largest concentration at any comparable range — with the US spot ETF cohort's average cost basis in the same band.The Fed decides Wednesday at 2:00 p.m. ET, with the Bank of England Thursday and the Bank of Japan Friday.

data.title: Japan’s Economic Revival Faces BOJ’s Fastest Hike Cycle Since Bubble Burst
data.description: Japan’s shift from a dormant economic giant to a magnet for growth and investment is set to face its fastest sequence of interest-rate increases since Tokyo’s asset bubble burst more than a generation ago, according to Bloomberg.
